title: Investing for Beginners
subtitle: Demystify index funds, stocks, and the principles of long-term investing.

steps.content: Investing is the bridge between working for money and having your money work for you.
steps.tip: Over 30-year horizons, broad stock indexes have historically averaged roughly 7-10% annual returns.

steps.title: Core Asset Classes
steps.content:
Stocks: You own a fraction of a business. If it expands and profits, your shares grow in value.

Bonds: You lend money to governments or companies in return for predictable fixed interest payments.

Index Funds (ETFs): A single basket containing hundreds or thousands of stocks (like the S&P 500) all in one package.
steps.highlight: Index funds provide instant diversification across hundreds of companies.

steps.question: What is the primary advantage of investing in a broad index fund (like an S&P 500 ETF)?
steps.hint: Index funds spread your money across hundreds of companies, providing instant diversification at low cost.

options.text: Instant diversification across hundreds of companies at very low management cost
options.explanation: Diversification protects you if any single individual company underperforms.
No legitimate stock market investment guarantees immediate short-term returns.

options.text: Exemption from all federal and state taxes automatically
options.explanation: Taxes depend on account type (like Roth IRA or taxable brokerage), not the index fund itself.

steps.title: Dollar-Cost Averaging (DCA)
steps.content:
Instead of trying to guess whether the stock market will rise or fall tomorrow, Dollar-Cost Averaging involves investing a fixed dollar amount on a consistent schedule (such as $200 on the 1st of every month).

When prices dip, you automatically buy more shares; when prices rise, you buy fewer.
steps.highlight: Time in the market beats timing the market.

steps.question: Why is Dollar-Cost Averaging (DCA) recommended over attempting to time the market?
steps.hint: DCA automates regular contributions on a schedule, eliminating emotional guesswork and buying more shares when prices dip.

options.text: It removes emotional guesswork and automatically buys more shares when prices are discounted
options.explanation: DCA builds disciplined wealth accumulation without stress over short-term market fluctuations.

options.text: It allows you to trade options with leverage
options.explanation: DCA is a patient, long-term strategy, the opposite of high-risk speculative trading.

options.text: It forces companies to pay double dividends
options.explanation: Company dividends are determined by corporate boards, not individual investment schedules.

steps.title: Investing Foundations Set
steps.content: You understand asset classes, the power of broad index funds, and why regular automated investing leads to financial independence.
